chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān al-Nahdī and Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About the Imam of a people who is afflicted with janābah during travel, and he does not have enough water with him for ghusl (ritual bath): should some of them perform wudu (ablution) and lead them in salat (prayer)?
He عليه السلام said: 'No. Rather, the junub should perform tayammum and lead them in salat (prayer), for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made earth a purifier just as He has made water a purifier.'

key_terms.التُّرَابَ: earth/dust, the material used for tayammum
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the circumstance in which the ruling is being asked about
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: the person in a state of janābah
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the normal means of ritual purification
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.لِلْغُسْلِ: for ghusl (ritual bath), the required purification from janābah
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, dry ablution as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: Can a junub traveler perform tayammum and lead the prayer if there is not enough water for ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum when a person in a state of janābah is traveling and lacks sufficient water for ghusl (ritual bath). It establishes that the junub may perform tayammum and lead the congregation in salat (prayer), because Allah has made earth a valid means of taharah just as He made water a means of purification.
